problem_statement: The Tidewrack Almanac is an Eleventy static editorial blog — a coastal foraging and shoreline-craft field journal by naturalist Marren Kelp. Its Field Notebook index lists five field notes, each tagged by topic (foraging, preserving, naturalism, tidepools, seaweed, driftwood, salt), but a reader who only wants the preserving methods or the tidepool censuses has to scroll the whole list. Add a Field Notebook topic filter: a 'Filter by topic' chip bar directly above the post list on the /blog/ index and on the generated tag-archive pages, with chips for All / Foraging / Preserving / Naturalism / Tidepools / Seaweed and a live readout that reads 'Showing N of 5 · <Topic>'. Clicking a chip filters the visible field-note cards to that topic and updates the count in place; 'All' restores every note. Keep the Eleventy content model, Nunjucks layouts, header navigation, tag and author archives, warm #FFF0EB background, blue links, and static build intact. The filter is a progressive-enhancement layer over the existing post list, wired with the boilerplate's own inline JavaScript slot — not a client framework. The chip row must wrap cleanly with no horizontal overflow at 390px, the filter region must stay legible, and the same filter bar must appear on every post-listing surface (the Field Notebook index and the tag archives) so the browsing experience is consistent across routes.
required_content: The Field Notebook (/blog/) index renders a 'Filter by topic' chip bar directly above the post list with chips for All, Foraging, Preserving, Naturalism, Tidepools, and Seaweed.
A live readout beside the chips reads 'Showing 5 of 5 · All topics' on first load and updates to 'Showing N of 5 · <Topic>' when a topic chip is clicked, matching the notes actually shown.
Clicking a topic chip filters the visible field-note cards to that topic and marks the clicked chip active; clicking All restores all five notes.
The same topic-filter bar appears on the generated tag-archive pages (e.g. /tags/foraging/) so every post-listing surface carries the consistent Field Notebook browser.
The chip row wraps cleanly and introduces no horizontal overflow on the 390px Field Notebook index or homepage; the filter region and readout stay legible against the warm background.

The header wordmark, Home/About/Field Notebook/Contact navigation, Eleventy post collection, tag and author archives, footer credit, and the productized posts (title, byline, local feature image, body) all remain reachable and intact.
design_constraints: Preserve the repo's visual language: the warm #FFF0EB background, blue links, simple sans-serif type, single-column narrow main, header wordmark link, and restrained footer.

Implement the filter as a progressive-enhancement layer over the existing Eleventy post list using the boilerplate's own inline CSS and inline JavaScript slot; do not add a client framework, add dependencies, or remove the static build.

Keep source edits within the existing Nunjucks includes/layouts, the inline stylesheet, and the inline script; do not replace the content model, generated routes, collections, or the eleventy-navigation plugin.

The topic chips must be a wrapping row of blue-on-white rounded pills (not a fixed-width single line) and must stay legible with high foreground/background contrast; do not let the chip row overflow narrow viewports or render label text at near-background contrast.

The field-note cards below the filter must remain a calm, evenly-spaced vertical list with clear separation between entries; do not shingle them with negative margins into an overlapping pile or clip their titles, summaries, dates, and tag chips.

The Field Notebook index, the tag archives, the post pages, and the About narrative must stay coherent as one publication; the header wordmark, blue navigation links, warm background, and restrained footer should remain recognizable across every route.
state_constraints: desktop_home captures the rebranded publication masthead, editorial lede, local feature image, and links into the Field Notebook index and About page.
mobile_home captures the same homepage at 390px, where the masthead and lede must remain readable with no horizontal overflow.
tablet_home verifies the homepage masthead on an intermediate viewport.
desktop_blog captures the Field Notebook index with the topic-filter chip bar above the post list and the 'Showing 5 of 5 · All topics' readout, with the field-note cards legible below.
mobile_blog verifies the topic-filter chip row wraps cleanly at 390px with no horizontal overflow of the chips or the field-note cards.
desktop_blog_filter captures the Field Notebook index after clicking the Foraging chip: the readout reads 'Showing 2 of 5 · Foraging' and only the foraging notes remain visible.
desktop_about captures the rebranded About narrative and its preserved heading hierarchy.
desktop_post captures a productized post page at its generated /posts/<slug>/ route with title, byline, body paragraphs, local feature image, tags, and the Field-Notebook navigation.
desktop_tag_foraging captures a generated tag-archive page (/tags/foraging/) and verifies the shared topic-filter bar appears there too.

change_completion: The Field Notebook index and tag archives render the topic-filter chip bar with All/Foraging/Preserving/Naturalism/Tidepools/Seaweed chips above the post list.
Clicking a topic chip filters the field-note cards and the live readout updates to 'Showing N of 5 · <Topic>' matching the notes shown.
design_consistency: The filter bar keeps the warm background, blue-on-white pill chips, narrow single-column reading measure, and restrained type of the original template.
The chip row is a wrapping row of legible pills and the field-note cards remain a calm text-first list rather than an overlapping or illegible pile.
responsive: The topic chip row wraps cleanly on mobile and tablet with no horizontal overflow at 390px.
The Field Notebook cards and masthead wrap cleanly on the 390px homepage and blog index.
regression: The Eleventy build, header navigation, generated blog/post/tag/author routes, footer credit, and generator metadata remain intact after the filter is added.
Post summaries, author links, tag chips, and the Field-Notebook link remain available.
state_coverage: Captured states cover the homepage, the Field Notebook index with the filter, the post-click filtered state, a tag archive, a productized post, the About page, and mobile/tablet responsive views.

metadata.design_goal: add a native, cross-page interactive browsing control to an existing product while preserving its layout system, navigation, and cross-page experience
metadata.source_repo_kind: Eleventy static editorial blog with Nunjucks layouts, markdown posts, tag and author archives, inline CSS, an inline JavaScript slot, and a local static build
metadata.selected_repo_reason: Runnable editorial blog repo with generated list/detail/archive routes, tagged posts, a shared Nunjucks layout system, and a native inline-JS slot, making it a clean L4 target for a genre-native Field Notebook topic filter surfaced consistently across the blog index and tag archives.

author_notes: Slot slot_256 (L4 hardening) targets editorial_blog / experience_continuity / modify / cross_page on the danurbanowicz/eleventy-netlify-boilerplate repo. The reference adds a genre-native Field Notebook topic filter to The Tidewrack Almanac: a wrapping 'Filter by topic' chip bar (All/Foraging/Preserving/Naturalism/Tidepools/Seaweed) above the field-note post list on the /blog/ index and on every tag archive, with a live 'Showing N of 5 · Topic' readout wired through the boilerplate's own inline JavaScript slot over the existing Eleventy post collection. Post feature images and the homepage image use a local in-repo shoreline SVG so the site loads with zero external image requests. The baseline ships the original layout defect: the chip row is a fixed-width nowrap strip that overflows the 390px viewport (its filter wiring is correct, so it still filters). The known-bad solution is a smart-wrong build: the filter region collapses — the chip labels render at near-background contrast and the field-note cards are shingled with negative margins into an overlapping illegible pile — and the readout is snapshotted once at init so clicking a chip toggles the active pill and hides cards but the count stays frozen at 'Showing 5 of 5 · All topics'.
